context.body: Abner the son of Ner, and the servants of Ishbosheth the son of Saul, went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Champions meet, battle spreads, Asahel pursues Abner and is killed, Joab continues until Abner calls for the sword to stop consuming.
observations.label: A contest at Gibeon becomes civil bloodshed: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps Abner, Joab, Asahel, Benjamin, and David’s servants, Gibeon, the field, and Bethlehem burial ground, meeting, competing, pursuing, warning, killing, rallying, and ceasing visible within David's story or later memory.

payload.posture: Read 2 Samuel 2:12–32 as its own judah, conflict, and unification David setting before carrying its language into another source.
